transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess what brings me in is I can’t get this thought out of my head. I’ve been an electrician for years, you know, and people always acted like I was the guy who knew what was safe, what wasn’t. I used to be real particular about wiring, grounding, all that stuff—my brother used to joke I’d check a toaster like it was a hospital generator.

But… if all those years, all that knowing how things are supposed to work, couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then what good is it? I keep thinking I’m a danger to anyone who works with me, or even anyone living under my roof. Like maybe being around me puts people at risk. That’s why I’m here, I think. I can’t shake that.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals to try and alleviate these thoughts about being a danger to others?

I don’t know… rituals, like, I’m not sure I’d call it that. I mean, I’ve always checked things more than most people, but that was the job, you know? You don’t just trust a breaker because someone wrote “kitchen” on a panel in Sharpie in 1998.

But lately… I don’t know if it’s a ritual or just me trying to feel less like I’m gonna miss something. I’ll think about whether I left something unsafe, and then my mind kind of runs with it. Like even at the grocery store I’ll notice the ceiling lights buzzing and start thinking about who wired them, and then I’m back thinking about work, and my brother, and—sorry, I know that’s not what you asked.

I guess I’m not totally sure. I don’t have some set thing I do every time, if that’s what you mean.
Would you say these thoughts about being a danger to others come into your mind against your will?

Yeah… yeah, I’d say they do. It’s not like I sit down and decide to think about it.

I’ll be in the middle of wiring a panel, focused on what’s in front of me, and then out of nowhere it’s like the whole job site drops out from under me. Or I’ll hear my nephew shut the garage door, just a normal sound, and suddenly I’m right back there—smelling smoke, seeing my brother. It just… comes in. I don’t want it there.

And then I’m not really in the room anymore, if that makes sense. I mean, I know I am, but my head’s somewhere else. Like when you hear a breaker pop and everyone looks at the electrician, like you’re supposed to have the answer—sorry, I’m getting off track. But yes. It comes in against my will.
Do you feel like you have to do something to make these thoughts about being a danger to others go away?

I don’t know… “have to” is the part I get stuck on. I mean, sometimes I’ll want to do something, just to get my head to quiet down, but I don’t know if that’s the same as having to.

It’s like when you’re on a job and someone says, “Did you tighten that lug?” and even if you know you did, now the question’s in your head, and then you’re thinking about every panel you ever worked on. My old foreman used to say, “Trust your hands,” which sounds nice until your hands are the thing you don’t trust anymore.

But… I don’t really know what I’m supposed to do to make it go away. There isn’t one thing that fixes it. Sometimes I just kind of get stuck with it.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to perform specific actions when these thoughts of being a danger to others occur?

Overwhelming urge… I don’t know. I’m not sure I’d call it that.

Sometimes I get restless, like I should be doing something, but it’s not always a specific action, if that makes sense. It’s not like, “I have to tap the wall three times” or anything like that. It’s more like my brain starts looking for a way out, like if I could just figure out the one thing I missed, then maybe I’d calm down.

But then I start thinking about work again, and how on some jobs you’d check behind the drywall before anyone closed it up, because once it’s sealed you can’t see what’s in there anymore, and that always bothered me—sorry. I’m doing it again.

So… no, I don’t think it’s a specific urge exactly. More just this uncomfortable feeling that I need to do something, but I don’t know what.
Do you find these thoughts about being a danger to others to be very distressing when they occur?

Yeah… very distressing. That’s probably the main reason I came in, honestly.

I can’t shake this thought that if all my years doing electrical work—knowing what to check, knowing what’s safe, knowing what can go wrong—if that still couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then what does that say about me? Like maybe I’m dangerous to anybody who works with me, or even anybody living under the same roof as me.

And I know that sounds… I don’t know. I can hear how it sounds. But when it hits, it’s not some passing worry. It feels like proof, almost. Like every outlet, every breaker, every little mistake a person could make—sorry, I’m getting into the work stuff again. But yes. It really upsets me. It makes me feel like I can’t trust myself around people.
Do you feel like you are trying to neutralize or counteract these thoughts about being a danger to others with other thoughts or actions?

I’m not sure. “Neutralize” sounds like… I don’t know, like there’s supposed to be some trick to cancel it out.

I guess I try to think my way through it sometimes, like telling myself, “You know how to do the work, you’re careful,” that kind of thing. But then that turns into going over details, and then I’m back in the weeds, thinking about whether a junction box was accessible or whether somebody used the wrong gauge wire years ago—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

Actions… I don’t know that I have a clear thing I do to counteract it. It’s more like I’m trying to argue with the thought in my head, and it doesn’t really work. It just keeps circling.
Do you feel like you are compelled to repeat certain behaviors when you have these distressing thoughts about being a danger to others?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying, like repeating a behavior over and over because I have to.

I might check something again if I’m already there, but I’m an electrician, so checking things is just part of the job, you know? That’s where I get tangled up, because a good electrician checks his work. My old foreman used to say if you don’t test it, you didn’t do it, and that kind of sticks in your head.

But when the thought hits, I don’t notice myself doing some specific repeated thing. It’s more like I get stuck thinking about it. I go in circles in my head, but behavior-wise… no, I’m not sure there’s a certain thing I repeat.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are a part of yourself or are they something that feels foreign to you?

I don’t know if I’d call them foreign. They feel like… they feel like me, but the worst version of what I believe about myself, if that makes sense.

Like I came in because I can’t shake this idea that if all my years doing electrical work, all the training and habits and knowing what to look for—if that still couldn’t keep my own brother safe—then maybe I’m just a danger. To anybody on a job with me, anybody in my house. And then I start thinking about every little thing, like panels and outlets and whether someone overlooked something, and—sorry, I’m wandering.

But no, it doesn’t feel like some random thought dropped into my head from outside. It feels like something I believe about myself when I’m at my worst, and that’s what scares me.
Do these thoughts about being a danger to others feel like they are inconsistent with your own beliefs and values?

Yeah… I mean, yes and no. It doesn’t match what I want to be, if that’s what you mean. I’ve always tried to be careful. Being an electrician, you don’t get to be sloppy and just hope nobody notices. You check things, you think about who’s going to use it later, kids in a house, guys on a job site, whoever.

But the thought itself… it feels hard to argue with. I came in because I can’t shake this idea that if all my years doing electrical work couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody working with me or living under my roof. And then I start thinking about all the places I’ve worked, all the panels I’ve touched, and—sorry, I know I’m getting off track.

So, inconsistent with my values? Yes, because I don’t want to hurt anyone. But it also feels like this awful truth about me that I can’t get away from.
Do these thoughts about being a danger to others keep coming back to you throughout the day?

Yeah… they do. It’s not like I sit down and decide to think about it, it just comes back on me during the day.

I’ll be doing something normal, or thinking about a job, and then it’s right there again: if all those years as an electrician, all the training, all the times I was careful… if that still didn’t keep my own brother safe, then what does that make me? Then I start thinking I’m a danger to anybody working next to me, or anybody living under my roof.

And I know that’s kind of the same thing I keep saying, but it loops back around. I can be trying to focus on something else and there it is again.
Do you feel like you must perform a specific action when these thoughts about being a danger to others occur, such as checking something a certain number of times?

I’m not sure I do it in a set way, like… I don’t have a number in my head or anything like that. It’s more that when the thought hits, I kind of start looking around or thinking back over things, trying to make sure I didn’t miss something.

But specific action… I don’t know. I mean, in electrical work you check things anyway, that’s just part of it. My old foreman used to say if you’re not willing to check your work, you shouldn’t be touching wires at all, and that stuck with me. So it’s hard for me to separate what’s normal from what’s me getting wound up.

I don’t think it’s like “I have to check it seven times” or anything. It’s more this pressure in my head, like I should make sure, but I couldn’t tell you it’s a certain routine.
Do you want to have these thoughts about being a danger to others?

No. No, I don’t want them.

I mean, who would want to walk around thinking they’re dangerous to people? I came in because I can’t shake it, not because I’m choosing it. It’s just… if all my years as an electrician, all that being careful, checking work, knowing what can happen if you miss something—if that couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then my head goes straight to, “Maybe I’m a danger to anybody who works with me or lives under my roof.”

And I know you asked if I want the thoughts, and the answer is no. I’d give a lot not to have them. They just keep showing up like they’ve got a right to be there.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are something you're actively trying to think about, or are they intrusive and unwelcome?

They’re intrusive. Unwelcome. I’m not sitting there trying to think them up.

It’s more like… I’ll be doing something else and then my mind drags me back to it. I came in because I can’t shake this thought that if all my years working as an electrician, all that training and being careful, still couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody who works beside me or lives under my roof.

And I know that sounds like I’m circling the same drain again, but that’s what it feels like. It just keeps coming back whether I want it there or not.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are in line with your own identity and how you see yourself?

No… I mean, it doesn’t feel like who I used to think I was.

I’ve always seen myself as careful. That was kind of the whole thing with electrical work—you don’t rush, you don’t assume, you check because people can get hurt. I used to take some pride in that, honestly. My brother used to joke that I’d check a light switch like I was defusing a bomb, and… sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

The thought doesn’t fit with how I want to see myself, but it’s gotten tangled up in how I do see myself now. I came in because I can’t shake this idea that if all those years of being an electrician, being careful, still didn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody who works with me or lives under my roof. So no, it’s not in line with who I want to be, but it’s starting to feel like maybe that’s who I am.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are a part of your own beliefs and values, or do they go against what you believe about yourself?

They go against what I used to believe about myself, yeah. I mean, I’ve always believed I was careful. That was the job, you know—measure twice, shut the power off, check the panel, don’t cut corners. I used to get on younger guys about that, probably annoyed them half to death.

But now… I don’t know. I came in because I can’t shake the thought that if all my years as an electrician, all that caution and knowing better, couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody who works with me or lives under my roof.

So it’s not a value of mine. I don’t want to hurt anybody. That’s the whole point. But the thought keeps pressing on me like maybe it’s true anyway.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are something that you would consider to be a part of your own personality or values?

No, I wouldn’t say it’s part of my values. That’s the thing—I spent my whole working life trying to be the guy who kept things safe. Electrician work, you know, it’s not like fixing a squeaky cabinet. You mess up and somebody can get killed, so you learn to be careful.

But now it’s like… I came in because I can’t shake this thought that if all those years doing that, all those years being careful, still couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody who works next to me or lives under my roof.

So no, it’s not who I want to be. It doesn’t feel like a value. It feels like something that’s gotten stuck to me.
Have these thoughts about being a danger to others interfered with your ability to work or interact with your family and friends?

Yeah… it has. Work especially.

I mean, I used to be the guy people wanted on a job because I was careful, and now it’s like the opposite. My work’s been slipping. Not like I forgot how to wire something, but I’m second-guessing, getting tense, checking things in a way that makes everyone else nervous. Apprentices don’t want to pair with me anymore, which… that stings, because I used to teach those guys little tricks, like how to label runs clean so the next poor bastard doesn’t hate you.

And there was this solar job—I got pulled off it after a confrontation. They said I wasn’t safe to have on site. Hearing that… I don’t know. That kind of confirmed the thing I’m scared of, I guess.

With family and friends, I’m not sure how to answer cleanly. I’m not exactly easy to be around lately. But work, yeah, it’s gotten bad.
Do you feel like you're mentally replaying the events surrounding your brother's accident over and over again?

Yeah. I mean, not like I sit down and decide to think about it, but it happens.

I’ll be in the middle of wiring a panel, just doing something I’ve done a thousand times, and then something clicks wrong in my head and I’m not really there anymore. Or I’ll hear my nephew shut the garage door—just that heavy slam—and suddenly I’m right back smelling smoke and seeing my brother. It’s like the whole job site drops out from under me.

And then I’ll catch myself staring at the same breaker or the same screw for too long. I know I’m supposed to keep moving, but my head’s back there. It’s not useful remembering, you know? It’s just… replaying.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are directly related to your brother's accident?

Yeah. I mean… that’s where it comes from, I think.

If I’d been some careless guy my whole life, maybe it would make a different kind of sense. But I was an electrician for years, and the whole point was keeping people safe—checking things, not cutting corners, making sure nobody got hurt because of something I missed. And then my brother… I couldn’t keep him safe.

So my head goes, well, if all that experience and all that caution still wasn’t enough for him, then what does that make me around anyone else? Guys on a job with me, people in my house… even just normal stuff, I start thinking I’m the dangerous part of the room.

Sorry, I’m going off a little. But yeah. It’s tied straight to what happened with him.

My old foreman used to say if you’re not willing to check your work, you shouldn’t be touching wires at all, and that stuck with me. I don’t think it’s like “I have to check it seven times” or anything. It’s more this pressure in my head, like I should make sure, but I couldn’t tell you it’s a certain routine.

patient.answer:
Yeah. I mean… that’s where it comes from, I think.

If I’d been some careless guy my whole life, maybe it would make a different kind of sense.
